problem: Let $p=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 5\end{aligned}]$ and $q=[\begin{aligned}15 \\ \sqrt{2} \\ x\end{aligned}].$ Given that the scalar projection of $p$ onto $q$ is $0,$ find the value of $x.$

examples.knowledge_point: Projecting a Vector Onto a Perpendicular Vector
examples.problem: Let ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14098324/assets/e477b14c9148f4132c747a358e1e99f76d40df85b82c66d6e7dd38581b33913c.png) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14098324/assets/b17d86e3e395b2fd752f5529090c0a5e4e2fdce17642be5594bee98e8c47fed2.png) Find the scalar projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}.$
examples.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{c}_{z}{b}_{z}}{\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{0\cdot 2+0\cdot (-4)+1\cdot 0}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{0}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
